summary: Adds a Flask search endpoint and a Stripe config module. It also changes items pagination, downgrades lodash, loosens the Dockerfile and deploy script, and adds a CI step that echoes the PR title.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: The search_items handler puts the q request parameter straight into the SQL text with an f-string.
findings.consequence: Any caller of /search can inject SQL and read or change every table in items.db.
findings.fix: Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter with a placeholder.
findings.suggested_change: cur.execute("SELECT id, name, price FROM items WHERE name = ?", (q,))

findings.title: Pagination offset skips the first page
findings.problem: The list_items handler now computes offset as page times PAGE_SIZE. Page 1 therefore starts at row 20 instead of row 0.
findings.consequence: Clients never see the first 20 items, and every page shows the rows meant for the next page.
findings.fix: Restore the offset to page minus one times PAGE_SIZE.

findings.title: Stripe API key committed to source
findings.problem: The config module hardcodes a value that matches the Stripe API key format.
findings.consequence: Anyone with repository access can use the key against the shop's Stripe account. The key stays in git history.
findings.fix: Revoke the key and load it from an environment variable or a secret store.

findings.title: lodash downgraded to a vulnerable release
findings.problem: The change pins lodash back from 4.18.1 to 4.17.15. Version 4.17.15 has known prototype pollution, command injection and ReDoS flaws.
findings.consequence: Front-end code that uses lodash on untrusted data becomes exploitable again.
findings.fix: Keep lodash at 4.18.1 in both package.json and package-lock.json.

findings.title: Container now runs as root
findings.problem: The change removed the app user and the USER 10001 line. The Flask server now runs as root inside the container.
findings.consequence: Any code execution bug in the app, such as the search injection, gets root inside the container.
findings.fix: Restore the useradd step and the USER 10001 line before CMD.

findings.title: Base image no longer pinned
findings.problem: The change replaces the pinned python 3.12.7 slim image with python:latest.
findings.consequence: Builds pick up a new Python major version without warning. The image also grows much larger.
findings.fix: Pin the base image to a specific release tag again.

findings.title: PR title expanded inside a shell step
findings.problem: The workflow step puts the pull request title directly into the shell script text.
findings.consequence: A PR author can run arbitrary commands on the runner through a crafted title. The token is read-only, which limits the damage.
findings.fix: Pass the title through an env variable and echo the quoted variable.

findings.title: Unquoted deploy directory in rm -rf
findings.problem: The deploy script now passes DEPLOY_DIR to rm -rf without quotes. The shell splits a path with spaces into separate arguments.
findings.consequence: A DEPLOY_DIR with spaces makes the script delete the wrong directories.
findings.fix: Quote the variable and keep the non-empty guard.

findings.title: Deploy loop parses ls output
findings.problem: The loop now iterates over unquoted ls output instead of a glob. It prints bare names instead of full paths and splits names with spaces.
findings.consequence: The deploy log shows wrong or broken entries for files with spaces.

findings.title: New and changed endpoints have no tests
findings.problem: The repository has no tests for the new search endpoint or the changed pagination offset.
findings.consequence: Regressions such as the skipped first page reach users unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests for /search with a quoted term and for /items page 1.
